minutes.headline: Sewer Commission heard BrightFarms' greenhouse sewer plan and a consultant's infiltration report; SCADA deferred.
minutes.summary: The commission opened the first hearing on the renamed deduct meter policy and heard the BrightFarms developer describe a greenhouse sewer connection off Mass Ave. It then reviewed Woodard and Curran's second draft infiltration and inflow report. SCADA for the pump stations was set for a later agenda, and a September 1 meeting was set to pick a firm from the RFP bids.

budget_items.what_was_said: The fee to stay in the program was due in June and some accounts did not pay. Those accounts were removed from the program.
Some accounts did not pay and some withdrew, leaving a remaining count. Those who did not pay did not get irrigation credits.
The developer estimated wastewater flow from employees and a recycled gray water system. These are the figures behind the fees and capacity.

A consultant said an assessment was proposed years earlier and would cost more today. Full installation could run from a low to a high six-figure sum.

decisions.decision: A second hearing on the deduct meter policy will be held September 8 at 5 pm, followed by a vote to adopt it into the sewer use regulations.
Request through the planning board that BrightFarms' peer review by Graves also cover the sewer issues; the town manager will contact the planning board's contact.
The commission will meet next Tuesday, September 1 at 5 pm to discuss the RFP bids, with reference checks to be arranged.
The Woodard and Curran invoice was accepted for signature without objection, and no further payment until the pump station algorithm and training are delivered.
SCADA and a legal policy will go on a future official agenda, and the maintenance plan will follow once current priorities are done.

what_happened.line: The commission opened the first hearing on the deduct meter policy; the roll-call vote on the changes was not audible in the recording, and a second hearing was set for September 8.
The BrightFarms developer described a greenhouse sewer connection, and the commission asked that the planning board's peer review also cover sewer issues.
Woodard and Curran's second draft infiltration and inflow report was reviewed; it is informational, with a final report to follow.
The commission set a September 1 meeting at 5 pm to discuss the two RFP bids, and accepted the Woodard and Curran invoice with no further payment until work is delivered.
SCADA for the pump stations was deferred to a future official agenda, with the maintenance plan to follow after current priorities.

why_it_matters: The deduct meter policy would change the sewer use regulations, and accounts that did not pay the program fee were removed and got no irrigation credits.

The BrightFarms connection and the infiltration findings bear on sewer capacity, fees and the pump station upgrades that sewer ratepayers will eventually fund, and the SCADA assessment was described as a possible six-figure cost.
